maya: quick heads-up — experiment `cohorted-batch-v3` shows a perf regression when we enable cohort formation + per-cohort token budgets. p95 jumped for mid-length requests. :frowning:
aj: details? numbers? :eyes:
maya: short dump from canary run (host p95s aggregated):
```
  baseline (cohort off): p50 20ms, p95 82ms, p99 160ms
  cohorted-v3:         p50 22ms, p95 210ms, p99 480ms
  kv-hit-rate ~ unchanged (~68%)\n  kernel-switches/sec +2.1x on avg hosts
```

maya: repro steps: enable cohorted-batch-window=12ms, token-budget-per-cohort=48, cohort-hint=kv-prefetch, continuous-batcher on. small burst of many 64-token chat requests.

leon: interesting — kernel thrash looks like the thing. cohorting is making many small batches that force kernel selection to flip between small- and large-seq exec paths. that explains p95 spike.

sarah: are the batches actually smaller? what does batch size distribution look like?
maya: attached quick histogram (inlined): cohorts mostly 2-4 requests vs baseline 8-12. token budget cap causes early dispatch for cohorts, so small batches dominate.

kai: idea: probabilistic cohort ejects when queue depth > q_thresh. instead of hard eject we sample with p(eject) = clip((q - q0)/q_scale, 0..1) so we reduce kernel switching while still letting some cohorts through.
aj: +1. we tried deterministic eject before and it caused oscillation. probabilistic might smooth. have we simulated it?
maya: ran a micro-sim for 5m trace from prod-20:
```
  configs tested:
  - base: no-eject
  - det-eject: hard evict cohorts when q>120
  - prob-eject: p = (q-80)/200 clipped

  results (p95 median over hosts):
  base: 210ms
  det-eject: 175ms (but q oscillation, 10% request retries)
  prob-eject: 130ms, retries ~1.2%, kv-hit lost 0.5%
```

leon: nice — prob-eject reduces worst-case and keeps retries low. curious about impact on unit cost since smaller cohorts may reduce batching efficiency?
sarah: also we should consider kernel selection hysteresis: if a host recently chose small-kernel path, add a short suppress window to avoid immediate flips. together with prob-eject it might be stable.
kai: +1 on hysteresis. simple leaky token: when kernel-flip event occurs, tag host for 30ms with prefer-last-kernel bias. cheap to implement.
aj: what about soft-429 policy? if q keeps growing after prob-eject, we should switch to soft-429 with informative Retry-After and prefer fallback model variants. we saw earlier that soft limits keep availability better than hard 429 storms.
maya: canary observed a 429 spike when det-eject accidentally shrank effective throughput — deploy-bot rolled back one canary host.
deploy-bot: Canary 17 on us-west-2c rolled back at 2334501278 — 429 rate > 4% for 2m, auto-rollback triggered.

maya: action items imho:
- (A) implement prob-eject parameterized by q0/q_scale (kai + leon)
- (B) add kernel-selection hysteresis bias flag (leon)
- (C) wire soft-429 fallback throttle when q > hard_limit*0.85 (aj + sarah)
- (D) expand microbench trace set and run 1h end-to-end canary (maya)

leon: I'll draft a tiny runtime patch for hysteresis today. aiming for non-disruptive default off.
kai: I'll add prob-eject sim into the admission simulator and run overnight. will post numbers tomorrow.
aj: I'll update soft-429 policy doc and add metrics for Retry-After and fallback model hits.
sarah: I'll prepare an eval to ensure quality doesn't regress when using fallbacks.
maya: thanks — tagging :thumbsup: will follow up tomorrow with updated traces.

maya: quick config snippet for prob-eject we tested: 
```
admission:
  cohort_window_ms: 12
  token_budget_per_cohort: 48
  prob_eject:
    q0: 80
    q_scale: 200
    min_delay_ms: 5
```

leon: can we also emit a metric `admission.prob_eject.p` per-host so we can histogram effective p?
maya: yes, will add.

kai: one more note — we saw kernel switch count correlate strongly with CPU context switches. add host-level `kernel_switches/sec` to infra dashboard.
aj: creating a dashboard ticket.

maya: ok wrapping up here. let's keep thread for overnight sims. post results in morning. :coffee:
